correctness.rationale: Each inverse insertion (choose a missing value, lift child values, insert at a chosen position) produces a parent, and every deletion witness is obtained this way. Deduplication within each child bucket ensures each unordered pair receives one increment per distinct shared child. Thus the positive counters are exactly the desired intersection sizes, and omitted zero-overlap pairs cannot maximize. An independently written exact enumerator reproduced both incidence maps, all histograms, maxima (2,4,4,4,4,4), counts (6,1,4,18,96,600) and set equality of the entire extremal set with the proposed construction for n=4,...,8. The n=8 histogram for positive intersections of sizes 1,2,3,4 is (5521776,324432,320,600). For n=3, the four nonmonotone permutations have both children, giving six pairs. The four deletions in each block give the same four different local patterns. Contiguity in position preserves the outside pattern and consecutive block values leave each outside letter below or above the entire block, so the agreement extends to four different global children for all n>=4. All four block positions change and all other entries coincide, so the differing interval and value range are recoverable; counting the block as one atom gives (n-3)(n-3)!. This is no upper bound or classification past n=8. The frozen verify.py was inspected only. Independent replay: /workspace/branches/948953eb-8454-4d5c-9704-101c109a7983/independent_check.py (Python 3.12.3, NumPy 2.5.3; accepts --min-n and --max-n); the retained independent_check_n3-8.jsonl and independent_check_notes.md in that directory give the exact counts, set comparisons and recorded runs. Pair keys are exact uint32 with two 16-bit lexicographic IDs, safe since 8! < 2^16.
